# Deformation and Dynamic Modeling

Also called: Dynamic 3DGS, 4D Gaussian Splatting, Time-varying Gaussian Splatting

## Overview
Deformation and Dynamic Modeling extends the static [Gaussian Data Structure](#2273-gaussian-data-structure.md) to represent non-rigid motion and temporal changes in scenes. It solves the problem of rendering dynamic content by mapping static canonical Gaussian parameters to time-varying states via a deformation field. Unlike static [splatting](#23-splatting.md), it introduces a temporal dimension $t$ to the rendering pipeline, allowing for real-time synthesis of arbitrary time slices. It differs from sibling methods like [GSPull](2773-gspull.md) (which focuses on pull-based rendering optimization) and [SLAM and Tracking](6236-slam-and-tracking.md) (which focuses on camera pose estimation) by explicitly modeling the geometric evolution of the primitives themselves.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family decompose the scene into a static canonical representation and a time-dependent deformation field. The core mechanism involves storing canonical Gaussian parameters $\mathbf{c}_i = (\boldsymbol{\mu}_i, \mathbf{q}_i, \mathbf{s}_i, \alpha_i, \mathbf{c}_{SH,i})$ and computing time-varying parameters $\mathbf{c}_i(t)$ for rendering.

The deformation is typically predicted by a network $\mathcal{F}_{\theta}$ or a control mechanism that outputs deltas $(\Delta\boldsymbol{\mu}, \Delta\mathbf{q}, \Delta\mathbf{s})$. The updated parameters are computed as:
$$ \boldsymbol{\mu}_i(t) = \boldsymbol{\mu}_i + \Delta\boldsymbol{\mu}_i $$
$$ \mathbf{q}_i(t) = \text{Normalize}(\mathbf{q}_i \otimes \Delta\mathbf{q}_i) $$
$$ \mathbf{s}_i(t) = \mathbf{s}_i + \Delta\mathbf{s}_i $$
where $\otimes$ denotes [quaternion multiplication](#3474-quaternion-operations.md) [G]. The input to the deformation predictor usually includes the canonical features and the time parameter $t$, often normalized to $[0, 1]$ [G].

## Subtopics

### [Sparse-Controlled 3D Gaussian Splatting](6145-sparse-controlled-3d-gaussian-splatting.md)
[SC-GS](#6145-sparse-controlled-3d-gaussian-splatting.md) allows users to edit dynamic scenes by providing sparse control points that drive deformation via a learned prior. It uses influence weights to propagate edits, offering a compact and editable representation compared to per-Gaussian networks.

### [Deformable 3DGS](6866-deformable-3dgs.md)
[Deformable 3DGS](#6866-deformable-3dgs.md) applies a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) deformation network to per-Gaussian features over time. It maps canonical features and time to displacement, rotation, and scale updates, relying on a learned MLP rather than compact geometric encoders.

#### D-MiSo
D-MiSo is a motion-aware optimization method using sparse control trajectories [S1, unofficial]. It focuses on optimizing the [Gaussian set](#2074-gaussianset-data-structure.md) based on motion cues derived from sparse trajectories rather than dense temporal fields.

## Background
The concept of dynamic 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) emerged as an extension of the original static 3DGS to handle video and dynamic scenes. Early approaches focused on per-frame optimization, which was computationally expensive. The shift to canonical space with deformation fields allowed for real-time rendering of dynamic content. Key developments include methods using MLPs for deformation [S1, unofficial] and sparse control points for editing [S2, unofficial]. The field also includes variants like 4D-Rotor Gaussian Splatting and [GaussianFlow](#6149-gaussianflow.md) [S1, unofficial].
